title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 66-69 of the 'Longue Marche' notes, around 1981): Grothendieck is building an anabelian dictionary between schemes over a field K of finite type over Q and profinite group extensions E_X -> Gal(K̄/K).

The argument so far: by Artin's theory of elementary fibrations ('good neighbourhoods', SGA 4 XI), every point of a smooth X over K has a fundamental system of Zariski neighbourhoods U. Each such U is an 'elementary model': a tower of successive fibrations whose fibres are either curves of genus 0 with punctures (type (0,ν)) or finite étale covers of such. These U are étale K(π,1)'s, so each is faithfully encoded by an extension of profinite groups 1 -> π1(U_K̄) -> E_U -> G_K -> 1. Such extensions can be built step by step over Q, since every finitely generated extension of Q is a finite extension of a purely transcendental one.

This page draws the consequence. In principle any smooth K-scheme can be reconstructed by gluing such elementary pieces along open immersions. Open immersions of normal schemes correspond to surjections on fundamental groups, so the gluing data should also be expressible in group-extension terms.

Grothendieck then states a methodological dissatisfaction. Describing this gluing in the language of 'eternal extensions of profinite groups … or exterior actions' is unnatural. He wants a more geometric language, closer to intuition, in which 'rigid points' (points with coordinates in algebraic closures of fields, i.e. geometric points / Galois-orbits of K̄-points) play the leading role. He resolves to return to this.

He also wants to make explicit the whole étale topos of the schemes described by extensions, not just the K(π,1) 'piece'. Implicitly this is the full étale homotopy type of X, recovered by gluing the K(π,1) neighbourhoods.

The next page returns to concrete work: a section-criterion for when a rational section of a relative elementary U_S/S is everywhere defined, in terms of lifts E_K -> E_{U_S} factoring through E_S.
errors: No mathematical error, but there is a gap. Gluing K(π,1) pieces along open immersions determines the étale topos only if one also controls the overlaps and higher coherences. Concretely, intersections of elementary neighbourhoods are not themselves elementary and must be refined again, a hypercovering-type argument. The page only says 'en principe', so the gap is acknowledged implicitly.

The reconstruction of schemes (as opposed to their étale topoi) from the group data presupposes the anabelian Hom-conjecture for the elementary pieces. That conjecture was unproved at the time; it is now known in many cases (Mochizuki for curves; Hoshi–Mochizuki and Schmidt–Stix for higher dimension).

ideas.what: Every smooth variety over a finitely generated field of characteristic 0 has a basis of Zariski neighbourhoods that are elementary fibrations by (anabelian) curves, hence étale K(π,1)'s.
ideas.modern_name: Artin neighbourhoods / good neighbourhoods; hyperbolic polycurve neighbourhoods
ideas.usually_credited_to: M. Artin (SGA 4 XI, 1960s); anabelian use by Grothendieck, later Schmidt–Stix, Hoshi–Mochizuki
ideas.where_published: SGA 4 Exp. XI (Artin); anabelian use alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme and the 1983 letter to Faltings

ideas.what: Reconstructing smooth K-schemes, and their whole étale topos, by gluing elementary K(π,1) pieces described by profinite group extensions along open immersions.
ideas.modern_name: Anabelian geometry with étale homotopy types; reconstruction via Artin neighbourhoods
ideas.usually_credited_to: Schmidt–Stix, 'Anabelian geometry with étale homotopy types' (Annals 2016); idea attributed to Grothendieck's letter to Faltings
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983) mentions the étale topos / homotopy type of anabelian varieties; explicit gluing not published as far as I know

ideas.what: Wish for a geometric language replacing profinite group extensions and exterior actions, centred on 'rigid points' (geometric points with coordinates in algebraic closures).
ideas.modern_name: Groupoid / Galois-category language with base points; fundamental groupoid; Galois-orbits of geometric points (cf. the 'paquets de points base' of Esquisse)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA 1 groupoids; Esquisse: fundamental groupoid with tangential base points)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (groupoïdes fondamentaux, points base tangentiels); SGA 1 Exp. V

missed.claim: Grothendieck plans to describe the entire étale topos of a smooth scheme over K by gluing the anabelian K(π,1) pieces, which carry group-extension data, along open immersions. He also wants to reformulate the anabelian dictionary in a point-centred geometric language rather than one of profinite group extensions. Neither programme is carried out here.
missed.quote: expliciter les topos étales (pas seulement le "morceau" K(π,1)) tout entiers des schémas décrits ici par des extensions
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This anticipates the Schmidt–Stix approach to higher-dimensional anabelian geometry, using étale homotopy types and Artin neighbourhoods. Making the gluing explicit (a 'stack of extensions over the Zariski site') is still not cleanly formulated in the literature. It is mostly a documentation-of-priority point rather than new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: A methodological page. The idea that the full étale topos/homotopy type, glued from elementary K(π,1) neighbourhoods, is the right anabelian object in higher dimension was later realised by Schmidt–Stix. Grothendieck's general interest in it is known from the Faltings letter. The explicit 'gluing of extensions along open immersions' plan and the 'rigid points' language are a modest unpublished detail.
transcription_corrections: 'je sens[?] nettement[?]' reads as 'je sens nettement'.
'un langage[?] géométrique': the word is partly struck out/overwritten (a struck fragment precedes 'géométriques'); the meaning, a geometric language, is plausible.
'qui colle mieux à l'intuition géométrique': the manuscript has 'colle mieux : l'intuition géométrique'.
'(où coeff dans des clôtures algébriques de corps)': should read '(à coeff dans des clôtures algébriques de corps)'.
'Il me faudra y revenir dessus': the manuscript is 'Il me faudra y revenir dessus' (line break after 'revenir'); 'prépondérant' ends the preceding sentence.
